Definition: from G1223 and G1111; to complain throughout a crowd:--murmur.
BiblicalUsage: To murmur through a crowd is to complain until the whole company is buzzing with it. The Pharisees murmur when Jesus eats with publicans, and again when He goes to be the guest of Zacchaeus, and their complaint is always the same: He welcomes sinners.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that their murmuring is the sound of a heart that has forgotten grace; the Pharisees could not bear a Saviour who ate with sinners, and I must ask whether I ever murmur the same way when His mercy reaches someone I think unworthy.
